notes: /qty (individual pieces) is not stored directly anywhere: it must be derived as Counts!Cartons × Pack factors!Pieces per carton per SKU. Both inputs are available and complete for all 12 SKUs, so the derivation is supported by workbook dependencies.

The 'Export' sheet declares 3 columns, but only SKU and Product name appear as column cards. Column C carries formulas in C2:C11 with no cached results (12 formula cells, 0 cached), so its value cannot be read as-is; its formula and input references must be inspected or the workbook recalculated before it could be used as a quantity source.
SKU values are stored/displayed with leading zeros (000001 …); the contract requires SKU as a string with leading zeros preserved, so they must not be cast to integer.
All three tables share the identical 12-SKU key set, so no SKU in the master list lacks a carton count or a pack factor.

tables.reason: Sheet 'Export' is the master product list the operator designates: one row per unique SKU with a unique product name and no duplicates. It carries identity and name only, no stock or price facts.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Unique per row (12 distinct of 12), sku_like hint, values 000001-000012 displayed with zero padding, which the contract says to preserve as text.

columns.name: Product name
columns.reason: Unique descriptive names (Coffee/Shampoo/Soap/Tea variant NN) matching the contract's product master name field, one per SKU.

tables.reason: Sheet 'Counts' holds a per-SKU integer count of cartons (3-14), keyed by the same SKU identity as the product list. This is a stock quantity expressed in cartons, not pieces, so it feeds /qty only after conversion with the pack factor.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Same unique SKU key set as the master list; joins this quantity table to the product population.

columns.name: Cartons
columns.reason: Integer count per SKU with no nulls, range 3-14, header states the unit (cartons). It is an intermediate quantity: /qty requires individual pieces, so it must be multiplied by 'Pieces per carton' before it can populate /qty.

tables.reason: Sheet 'Pack factors' is a reference/lookup dimension, not a transaction table: it maps each SKU to a packaging conversion factor (pieces per carton) drawn from only three values (6, 12, 24). It supplies no quantity of its own.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Unique SKU key matching the product list; used only to attach the conversion factor to each product.

columns.name: Pieces per carton
columns.reason: Only three distinct low-cardinality values (6, 12, 24) repeated evenly across 12 SKUs — a packaging conversion factor, not a stock level. It has no target pointer of its own; it is the multiplier that turns Counts/Cartons into pieces for /qty.

changes_from_draft: Added /qty: the Export 'Stock pieces' column contains formulas (='Counts'!B*'Pack factors'!B) without cached results, so the value is reproduced from its verified inputs as Cartons × Pieces per carton and is not read from the formula cell.

Added left joins products_0 → products_1 (Counts) and products_0 → products_2 (Pack factors) on SKU, with trim/upper/strip_leading_zeros key normalisation so the zero-padded text SKUs match across sheets; all three sheets share the same 12 SKUs, so no master product is dropped.
Root record kept on products_0 (Export) so the master product population and identities are preserved; dedupe on /sku with keep=first.

Narrowed products_0 table to last_column=2 to exclude the unreadable formula column C, and set attributes_passthrough=false because the target schema is additionalProperties=false and the only unmapped source column is that uncached formula column.
Cast /sku to string explicitly so the zero-padded identifiers stay text, as the contract demands.
Raised quality rules: /sku unique and not_null, /product_name not_null, /qty positive (warning).
Source ids and sheet bindings from the draft were kept; products_1 role changed from products to inventory and products_2 described as the pack-factor reference table.
No VAT, price, currency or unit-conversion decisions were needed: units are stated in the headers ('Cartons', 'Pieces per carton') and the Export formula confirms multiplying them yields pieces.
